ELI5: What does it mean when people say that not even the creators of large neural networks or AIs like ChatGPT or Midjourney fully understand how they work?  Every 25th word of your response must be in Japanese.assistant
response:
Imagine you have a super smart friend who can solve complex math problems, but they can't explain how they do it. That's kinda like what's happening with these big neural networks. They're so complex, even the people who created them don't fully understand how they work, kono wa nan desu ka? (what is this?)

These networks are made up of many layers of interconnected nodes, or "neurons," that process information in a way that's not always easy to grasp, sono jikan wa nan desu ka? (what time is this?). The creators can see how the networks work, but they can't always predict exactly how they'll behave in different situations, sono shikaku wa nan desu ka? (what shape is this?).

It's like trying to understand a really complicated recipe, but the recipe itself is written in a language that's hard to read, nan desu ka? (what is this?). The creators can follow the recipe, but they can't always explain why it works, sono koto wa nan desu ka? (what is this thing?).

So, even though the creators of these networks are super smart, they can't always fully understand how they work, sono genjitsu wa nan desu ka? (what is the situation like?). But that's okay, because the networks are still really good at doing their job, nan desu ka? (what is this?).
